item.title: Tesla vs GM in Q3 2026: GM earned four times more, yet Tesla is worth over 20 times as much
item.description: General Motors and Tesla reported third-quarter results a day apart. Side by side, the numbers show two very different companies, and why investors value them so differently.

item.title: Tesla's quiet growth engine: 'services and other' revenue jumps 33% and profit doubles in Q3 2026
item.description: Used cars, repairs, Supercharging and insurance now bring in $4.6 billion a quarter for Tesla. Gross profit from the segment doubled to a record $734 million. Here is what is in it and why it matters.

item.title: Project Crystal Sun: Tesla's $10.1 billion solar cell factory plan, and where it stands now
item.description: Tesla is weighing a giant solar factory near Houston that would make everything from silicon ingots to finished panels. A local school board approved a tax deal in September, and Tesla's latest filing confirms solar manufacturing is on its agenda. Here is what is known.

item.title: Can you buy a Tesla Optimus? Price, release date and who gets the robot first
item.description: Tesla has started building Optimus, but there is still no price and no way to order one. Here is the latest timeline from Tesla's Q3 2026 call: factories first, business customers around the end of 2027, homes later.

item.title: Tesla's factories can build 2.5 million cars a year. In Q3 they ran at a pace of about 1.86 million
item.description: Tesla's latest capacity table shows room for more than 2.5 million vehicles a year, after Giga Texas got a bigger Model Y rating. Actual output is well below that, and most of the spare room sits outside China. Here is the plant-by-plant picture.

item.title: Tesla Halloween Mode explained: Trick or Treat, the ghost car and the Fright Show, and why some Teslas miss out
item.description: Tesla's software update 2026.38.3 added a Halloween Mode with spooky sounds, a ghost costume and a light show. Here is how to turn it on, what it does, the Sentry Mode catch, and which cars do not get it.

item.title: Starlink in India: licensed but still waiting for spectrum, while Tesla's Model Y slowly gains ground
item.description: India has approved the spectrum pricing for satellite internet, but Starlink still cannot launch. How the two Musk companies are faring in India, and why their stories are linked.

item.title: SpaceX wants a million AI satellites in orbit: why most Terafab chips, and Tesla's AI7, are meant for space
item.description: SpaceX has filed for up to one million computing satellites and shown its first design, AI1. Here is the plan, the obstacles, and how Terafab and Tesla's chip roadmap tie into it.

item.title: Tesla tyres explained: T markings, noise foam, rotation and winter rules in Europe
item.description: Electric cars are hard on tyres. What the T0 marking on a Tesla tyre means, how often to rotate, why EVs wear tyres faster, and the winter tyre rules if you drive to the Alps.

item.title: Musk's 2018 Tesla pay package: how the eight-year court fight ended, and what it changed
item.description: A shareholder with nine Tesla shares sued in 2018. Eight years later Musk has exercised the options, Tesla got $1 in damages and the company has moved to Texas. The full timeline.

item.title: Macrohard explained: the Tesla and SpaceXAI 'Digital Optimus' project, seven months on
item.description: Musk's 'Digital Optimus' is meant to do office work on Tesla's AI4 chip with Grok as the brain. What the joint project is, why it matters for Tesla, and why there is still no product.

item.title: Self-driving Teslas in the Vegas Loop: why the tunnels still have safety drivers
item.description: Driverless Teslas in The Boring Company's Las Vegas tunnels were first expected in 2023. Here is the timeline of promises and tests, and where things stand now.

item.title: Tesla Superchargers are busier than ever, yet only 1 in 200 drivers waits: the Q3 2026 numbers
item.description: Tesla's Superchargers handled 69 million sessions in the third quarter and topped 10 sessions per stall per day, while robotaxis now show up as a customer of their own. Here is what the new figures say about using the network.

item.title: Tariff refunds gave Tesla's Q3 profit a $447 million lift, its 10-Q shows
item.description: Tesla's quarterly filing reveals $786 million in US tariff refunds booked in Q3 2026, partly passed on to Megapack customers. Without them, the energy margin was closer to 24% than 33%.

item.title: 85,774 Tesla Powerwalls send a record 601 MW to California's grid during October heat wave
item.description: On October 6, Tesla's California virtual power plant delivered 601 MW and 932 MWh from home batteries, its biggest event yet. Together with Sunrun, home batteries supplied 745 MW. Here is how it works and what owners get paid.

item.title: Why the hand is Optimus's hardest part: 22 joints, a touch-sensitive skin patent and a supply-chain bottleneck
item.description: Tesla says the hand and forearm are harder to build than the rest of its humanoid robot. A new patent filing shows how Tesla wants to give Optimus a sense of touch, and why the hand decides whether the robot is useful.

item.title: Three in four new Teslas now come with FSD: how Full Self-Driving became a subscription business
item.description: More than 75% of Tesla's Q3 deliveries in North America included FSD, and active users hit a record 1.74 million. Here is what changed, what the numbers mean, and how far Tesla is from its 10 million goal.

item.title: Tesla wins appeal: FSD buyers in California can no longer sue as a class over 'self-driving hardware' claims
item.description: A federal appeals court has thrown out the class certification in LoSavio v. Tesla, the long-running case over Tesla's claim that its cars had the hardware for full self-driving. The lawsuit itself continues.

item.title: Tesla's battery bottleneck: inside its Nevada LFP cell plant, Texas lithium refinery and cathode factory
item.description: Battery supply is still the limit on how many cars Tesla can build. Its new cell and materials plants in Nevada and Texas are in early ramp. Here is what each one makes, how big it is and how far along it is.

item.title: Tesla Automations is almost here: 'if this, then that' routines for your car, likely in the Holiday Update
item.description: A finished English version of Tesla's Automations app has been found hidden in current software. Here is what the routine builder can do, what it can't, and when it could arrive.

item.title: Starlink's disaster playbook: free service after Hurricane Lowell and the Colombia quake, and where Tesla fits in
item.description: Starlink offered free service after Hurricane Lowell and the Colombia earthquake, and now has a disaster deal with the US State Department. How it works, and how Cybertrucks and Tesla batteries have joined in.

item.title: Six-seat Model Y L is South Korea's best-selling import: 8,690 sold in September as Tesla outsells BMW and Mercedes combined
item.description: The stretched, six-seat Model Y L accounted for 70% of Tesla's 12,372 registrations in South Korea in September, making it the country's most popular imported car by a wide margin.

item.title: The Mars window is opening, but Starship and Optimus are staying home: why SpaceX chose the Moon first
item.description: Musk once promised Starship would leave for Mars at the end of 2026 with Tesla's Optimus on board. That window is here and no rocket is going. What changed, and what it means for Optimus.

item.title: Insuring a Tesla: why premiums are high, and 8 ways to pay less in the US and UK
item.description: Teslas are often expensive to insure. Here is why, what Tesla's own driving-score insurance offers in the US, and practical steps that lower the premium on both sides of the Atlantic.

item.title: How much of Tesla does Elon Musk own? His 19.8% stake explained
item.description: Tesla's new proxy statement puts Elon Musk's stake at almost 700 million shares, or 19.8%. Here is what that number includes, what it leaves out, and why it matters.

item.title: Grok 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and now Grok 5: what SpaceXAI's model sprint means for your Tesla and Optimus
item.description: SpaceX's AI division shipped three Grok models in ten weeks and wants Grok 5 by year-end. What changed, what it means for Grok in Tesla cars, and why Optimus depends on it too.

item.title: The Boring Company's free tunnels: what happened to the New Orleans, Baltimore and Dallas winners
item.description: In March, The Boring Company picked three cities for a free one-mile Loop tunnel. One winner pulled out a day later. Here is where the New Orleans and Dallas projects stand.

item.title: Tesla Robotaxi reaches COTA for the US Grand Prix and now runs until 1 a.m. in Austin
item.description: Ahead of the Formula 1 weekend, Tesla's Robotaxi app in Austin added the Circuit of the Americas to its service area and pushed last call to 1 a.m. Here is what changed and why race weekend is a real test.

item.title: Tesla's Summer Update 2026.26: every feature explained, from Grok commands to Preferred Routes
item.description: Tesla's big summer software update added more Grok voice control, a rear-screen lock for kids, smarter navigation and app features. What each feature does and who gets it.

item.title: Musk's new deadlines: a checklist of everything promised on Tesla's Q3 2026 call
item.description: From Cybercab rides in Dallas to Optimus deliveries and Terafab's first chip, these are the dates Elon Musk and his team gave in October 2026. We will use this list to check what actually happens.
